title: Proper-support derived projection formula without quasi-compactness
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Derived tensor and pullback use K-flat resolutions with flat terms; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. Noetherian means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts. Coherent means quasi-coherent and, on Noetherian affine etale charts, associated to finitely generated modules. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. The support of a cohomology module is its closed locus of nonzero geometric stalks; it is proper over a base if its reduced induced closed subspace is proper over that base. Let $Y$ be Noetherian, let $f:X\to Y$ be locally of finite type and quasi-separated, and let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ have coherent cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, with each $\operatorname{Supp}H^i(E)$ proper over $Y$. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module $F$, there is a natural isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$
$$ (Rf_*E)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Y}F[0]\ \cong\ Rf_*\left(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}(f^{-1}F)[0]\right). $$
The tensor inside direct image carries its $\mathcal O_X$-module structure through the first factor. The displayed isomorphism is the canonical projection comparison $ (Rf_*E)\otimes^{\mathbf L}F\to Rf_*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}Lf^*F)$ followed by the canonical scalar-restriction tensor identification. No relative Tor condition, flatness or quasi-compactness of $f$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose $a\le b$ outside which $H^i(E)=0$, and put $T=\bigcup_{i=a}^b\operatorname{Supp}H^i(E)$. The finite-union assertion of [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-closed-operations] makes $T$ proper over $Y$. Thus $T$ is quasi-compact, since a proper morphism is quasi-compact and $Y$ is quasi-compact. Choose an etale scheme atlas of $X$ and cover it by affine opens. Their images are quasi-compact open subspaces by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. Finitely many cover $T$; their union is a quasi-compact open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ containing $T$ (take $U=\varnothing$ if $T=\varnothing$). Set $g=fj$. Since $f$ and $Y$ are quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] makes $X$ quasi-separated. The open subspace $U$ is quasi-separated as well: its diagonal is the base change of the diagonal of $X$ to $U\times U$. Now [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] makes $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. No quasi-compactness of $X$ or $f$ was used.

source.place: Tag 08IS, lemma-perfect-direct-image, support-union and quasi-compact-open reduction; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03E4, 03BZ, 03IR.

proof.text: Put $W=X\setminus T$. All cohomology sheaves of $E|_W$ vanish: exact etale restriction identifies them with $H^i(E)|_W$, whose geometric stalks vanish, and [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points] detects zero. Apply [lem-sfb-space-elementary-shriek-exact] to the open cover $(W,U)$ of $X$. Its overlap and $W$ terms vanish on $E$, so its exact functor sequence gives the canonical counit isomorphism $j_!(E|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}E$. The reduced complement of $W$ is contained in $U$, so this is an elementary distinguished square, and $E|_U$ is zero on $W\cap U$. By [lem-sfb-space-supported-etale-excision], $j_!(E|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_*(E|_U)$ is canonical. The composite $E\to Rj_*(E|_U)$ is the open-adjunction unit: its $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ transpose is the identity, by the normalization of the excision map and the triangular identity for $j_!\dashv j^*$. With the composition comparison of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], applying $Rf_*$ gives a natural isomorphism $a_E:Rf_*E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*(E|_U)$. This argument applies to every unbounded derived object zero on $W$.

source.place: Tag 08IS, support reduction; Tag 08GG, lemma-pushforward-with-support-in-open; Tag 08GV, lemma-exact-sequence-lower-shriek.

proof.text: Write $K=F[0]$ and $M=E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}^{\mathbf L}Lf^*K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and exact etale restriction and pullback composition in [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], $M|_W=(E|_W)\otimes^{\mathbf L}(Lf^*K)|_W=0$ and $M|_U\cong(E|_U)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg^*K$. Tensor with zero is zero: its K-flat representative is the zero complex. The preceding support argument therefore gives a natural isomorphism $a_M:Rf_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*((E|_U)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg^*K)$. In particular no boundedness or coherence of $M$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08IS, tensor displayed formula after the proper-support reduction; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product.

proof.text: Coherent cohomology is quasi-coherent by the stated convention. Exact restriction preserves quasi-coherence, as can be checked on the same etale affine charts in $U$. Thus $E|_U\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U)$, and $K=F[0]\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-derived-projection-formula] to $g$, which was verified qcqs in step 1. The definitions of the cited qcqs node are met: the diagonal $\Delta_g$ of $g$ is a monomorphism of sheaves, so its own diagonal is an isomorphism; hence $\Delta_g$ is quasi-separated, and $g$ is quasi-separated in the sense of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-derived-projection-formula]. If $C\to Y$ has $C$ quasi-compact, the last clause of [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] gives a surjective etale map $V\to C$ from a quasi-compact scheme, a finite disjoint union of affine schemes; $U\times_YV$ is then a finite union of the quasi-compact pullbacks to the affine pieces, quasi-compact by step 1, and surjects onto $|U\times_YC|$, so $U\times_YC$ is quasi-compact. Its canonical comparison $\pi_g:(Rg_*(E|_U))\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*((E|_U)\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lg^*K)$ is an isomorphism. Consequently $a_M^{-1}\pi_g(a_E\otimes1_K)$ is an isomorphism from $(Rf_*E)\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$ to $Rf_*M$.

source.place: Tag 08IN, lemma-cohomology-base-change; applied in Tag 08IS, first tensor equality.

proof.text: This composite is the specified projection comparison $\pi_f$, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of its endpoints. Write $E_U=j^*E$, $\eta_j,\varepsilon_j$ for the unit and counit of $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ (etale pullback is exact restriction, so $Lj^*=j^*$), $c:Rf_*Rj_*\cong Rg_*$ and $c':j^*Lf^*\cong Lg^*$ for the composition comparisons of [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], and $\mu_j:j^*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*K)\cong E_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*Lf^*K$ for the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. By construction in steps 2-3, $a_E=c\circ Rf_*(\eta_{j,E})$ and $a_M=Rg_*((1\otimes c')\mu_j)\circ c\circ Rf_*(\eta_{j,M})$. All projection maps $\pi_h$ here are the adjuncts of the counit on the first factor after the tensor comparison, as in [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition]. Its composition identity for $U\xrightarrow jX\xrightarrow fY$ gives, with $c,c'$ understood, $\pi_{g,E_U,K}=Rf_*(\pi_{j,E_U,Lf^*K})\circ\pi_{f,Rj_*E_U,K}$. Naturality of $\pi_f$ in its first argument along $\eta_{j,E}$ gives $\pi_{f,Rj_*E_U,K}\circ(Rf_*\eta_{j,E}\otimes1)=Rf_*(\eta_{j,E}\otimes1)\circ\pi_{f,E,K}$. It remains to see $\pi_{j,E_U,Lf^*K}\circ(\eta_{j,E}\otimes1)=Rj_*(\mu_j)\circ\eta_{j,M}$ as maps $M\to Rj_*(E_U\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*Lf^*K)$. Their $j^*\dashv Rj_*$ adjuncts are $(\varepsilon_{j,E_U}\otimes1)\mu_j\,j^*(\eta_{j,E}\otimes1)$, which by naturality of $\mu_j$ equals $((\varepsilon_{j,j^*E}\circ j^*\eta_{j,E})\otimes1)\mu_j=\mu_j$ by the triangular identity, and $\mu_j$. Combining, $c^{-1}\pi_g(a_E\otimes1_K)=Rf_*(Rj_*(\mu_j)\eta_{j,M})\circ\pi_f$, that is $\pi_g(a_E\otimes1_K)=a_M\pi_f$, after identifying $j^*Lf^*K$ with $Lg^*K$ by $c'$. Hence the composite in step 4 is $\pi_f$. Naturality in $E,K$ follows from that of $\pi_f$; although $U$ was chosen using $E$, the resulting map is the intrinsically defined $\pi_f$.

source.place: Tag 08IN, opening adjunction-mate definition; Tag 08IS, canonical support reduction; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map) composition of projection maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-relative-tensor-pullback] to the small etale ringed-topos morphism of $f$, with $E$ and $K=F[0]$. It identifies $M$ canonically with $E\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}^{\mathbf L}(f^{-1}F)[0]$, retaining the $\mathcal O_X$-action through $E$. Applying $Rf_*$ and composing this natural identification with the invertible $\pi_f$ from steps 4-5 gives exactly the displayed isomorphism in the item. The relative-tensor identification is valid without a Tor or flatness condition, and the support argument was valid for the possibly unbounded-below tensor object. Thus none of the excluded extra hypotheses has entered.
